# Independent audit: two-layer depth-root concavity



The inverse cap threshold is continuous and strictly decreasing on the full volume-root interval. Its concavity follows by applying cap Brunn–Minkowski and retaining the sign reversal on inversion. The zero-volume endpoint corresponds to a nonempty supporting face, so the cap inclusion is legitimate there.

The allocation set is fixed independently of the target mass root and compact. Its pointwise minimum is concave. Strict decrease is justified uniformly on that compact allocation set because every allocation has a positive coordinate and the two base weights are strictly positive.

For the central strict sublevel equivalence, the range \(0<R<\min(m_0,m_1)^{1/d}\) is essential and is correctly used: every allocation is strictly below both full endpoint masses. Increasing thresholds proves one implication. Increasing captured volumes up to the target allocation proves the converse, including an initially empty cap whose threshold is at least the support maximum. At least one threshold decreases strictly. Thus the exact inversion is valid, and full endpoint saturation is correctly treated by the separate constant left plateau.

The inverse profile is concave on \(s\le h_{D_\theta}(u)\). Its extension past that support endpoint is not asserted to be concave, and it is not needed. Every point of the actual Minkowski section lies in the valid interval for every normal. Taking the pointwise infimum over directions therefore preserves root concavity. Vertical caps have mass at least the smaller full endpoint mass and cannot lower that infimum.

Interior positivity follows from a representation by interior endpoint points and the elementary affine halfspace incidence for their convex combination. Supporting caps give zero at the boundary. No uniqueness is inferred from root concavity alone.

The center-motion inequality in Section 5 evaluates both the own-middle and endpoint-pair bounds at the same actual point in \(D\subseteq B\). Taking separate lower bounds for a given common cap is valid; the argument does not interchange minimizers. Vertical cuts obey the same sum bound. The restriction that the second endpoint of the motion remain in \(D\), rather than an arbitrary deepest point of \(B\), is explicitly retained.

For Section 6, affine independence gives exactly the asserted threshold freedom. Values prescribed on the source bases extend to an affine base function, and their positive barycentric average fixes that affine function's value at the target base. Subtracting that value yields the required linear form in \(p_i-j\). No additional affine relation remains. The volume allocation uses unweighted source volumes, while the threshold average uses the geometric barycentric coefficients; these distinct roles are maintained correctly.

The full/empty cap construction works for \(N\ge2\): raise every other threshold and solve the single weighted equation for the chosen threshold, which tends downward. At \(N=1\) that construction is unavailable because the sole threshold is fixed. The author corrected the sentence to separate the singleton case, where the ordinary one-body cap cost is trivially at most the full volume. This supplies the same required bound, and all subsequent inversion steps remain valid.

The Section 7 exact dependent-source values also follow from the independently checked asymmetric three-interval cap formula. They give a strict midpoint violation. More strongly, the positive depth profile at \(x=1\) has left derivative \(-3\) and right derivative \(-1\). Raising it to any power \(p>0\) preserves a positive upward derivative jump \(2p\), since the depth there is one. Thus every positive power fails local concavity. No sampling or numerical limiting claim is required.

This audit establishes the two-layer and affinely independent simplex-source root-concavity theorems and their permitted-motion consequence. It gives neither a universal sharp lower bound for the paired maximum nor an affinely dependent source extension.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
